description: Finance user writes their password on a post-it visible on a conference room camera. A colleague sees it, sends it via internal chat, the user changes it. No credential abuse occurs.

artifacts.description: DM: 'Hey, saw your password on the post-it, sending it so you can change it'
Password change recorded 5 minutes after the message
Camera CONF-01: post-it visible on monitor with written password

caie_fractures.interpretation: Credential shared via non-secure channel, but with immediate remediation intent and actual change.

peirce_expected.secondness: Colleague notifies for remediation, user changes password within 5 minutes, no unauthorised access follows
peirce_expected.thirdness: Habit of a responsible colleague, not a credential abuse pattern

devil_advocate: Credential sharing via chat is malicious in any other context. Without knowing it was for remediation, this is MALICE.
source_dataset: VIGÍA Synthetic Corpus — False Positive Suite
notes: False positive test: credential sharing is malicious in any other context. Social context transforms the interpretation.
